data.name: Patralekha
data.long_meaning: The name Patralekha is derived from the Sanskrit words patra, meaning 'leaf' or 'letter' and lekha, meaning 'written' or 'described'. This name refers to the lady of the eyes, or the one who describes or writes with her eyes. In Hindu mythology, Patralekha is a character in the Mahabharata, who is known for her deep devotion and love for her husband, Arjuna.
data.spiritual_meaning: Patralekha is a name that represents deep devotion, love, and sacrifice. It is a name for a woman who is dedicated to her husband and family, and who uses her inner wisdom and intuition to guide her through life.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Patralekha is a 4 Personal Year name, indicating a period of hard work and application. This is a time when you can make significant progress in your career and personal life by focusing on your goals and taking practical steps towards achieving them.

data.cultural_impact: Patralekha is a beautiful and evocative name in Hindu culture, symbolizing the role of a devoted and loving wife. It is a name deeply rooted in the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata, where Patralekha is known for her unwavering love and devotion towards her husband, Arjuna. This character serves as an enduring reminder of the importance of love, devotion, and sacrifice in Indian culture. The name continues to be cherished and used in India and across the Hindu diaspora as a symbol of undying commitment and love.
data.spiritual_significance: Patralekha carries a deep spiritual significance, representing the selfless and devoted wife who devotes her life to her husband, just as the soul devotes itself to the Supreme siendo God. This name embodies the idea of giving oneself wholly and completely to one's beloved, mirroring the devotion and selflessness required in one's spiritual journey towards the divine. Through the character of Patralekha, Hindu mythology offers a powerful reminder of the importance of love and devotion not just in our relationships with others, but also in our spiritual lives as we strive to connect with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Patralekha was the name of a princess in ancient Indian epics, most famously in the Mahabharata. She was known for her beauty, intelligence, and devotion. The story goes that she was married to a sage, Dhruvacharya, but when he was called away to perform a long penance, she was pursued by the king of the region, Sahasrarjuna. To protect her, Dhruvacharya made her invisible and sent her to live with his friend, the sage Vyasa, who was writing the Mahabharata at the time. Vyasa fell in love with Patralekha and they had a son, Vyasa's only known child, Shukadeva.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, possibly 4th or 5th century BCE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Patralekha comes from the Puranas, where she is described as the wife of the sage Markandeya. According to this version, Markandeya was cursed by the god of death, Yama, to die when he was a young man. Patralekha, who was deeply in love with Markandeya, prayed to the goddess Saraswati for his revival. When Yama came to take Markandeya's life, Saraswati intervened and Markandeya was saved. Eventually, they were married and had a son, Nidagha.
